heuristics.rule: When describing PGWP work authorization to employers, lead with 'no employer action required'
heuristics.condition: When filling out work authorization fields or responding to HR questions about visa status on PGWP...
heuristics.action: State explicitly that PGWP is an open work permit, valid for any employer, requiring no employer sponsorship, filing, or fees
heuristics.because: PGWP is employer-agnostic; the most common employer hesitation is fear of paperwork or cost, and preemptively eliminating that concern removes the friction before it arises

heuristics.rule: When targeting hiring managers on LinkedIn, filter for those who have posted technical content in the last 6 months
heuristics.condition: When doing cold outreach to hiring managers on LinkedIn...
heuristics.action: Search for SWE/DE Manager titles at the target company, then filter for those who have been active on LinkedIn recently — they are more likely to respond
heuristics.because: Active LinkedIn users signal openness to platform engagement; inactive profiles are unlikely to respond regardless of message quality

heuristics.rule: Do not invest time challenging 'citizens/PR only' job postings
heuristics.condition: When encountering a job posting or HR response stating they only hire citizens or permanent residents...
heuristics.action: Move on rather than attempting to change their position or pursue a complaint
heuristics.because: While the Canadian Human Rights Act has provisions against citizenship-based discrimination, enforcement is inconsistent and the cost of pursuing a complaint is high relative to the benefit for a job seeker in an active search

heuristics.rule: Prioritize alumni network outreach before applying through job boards
heuristics.condition: When beginning a job search in Canada as an international student...
heuristics.action: Systematically work through the school's alumni directory before relying on LinkedIn Easy Apply or Indeed
heuristics.because: The Canadian job market is smaller than the US market, which increases the density of alumni connections and the likelihood that any given alumnus is willing to help — multiple commenters corroborate that alumni referral yields dramatically higher interview conversion

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employers — especially smaller ones — may informally factor in how long a candidate can work without any additional action; a 3-year PGWP signals more runway than a 1-year permit and reduces implicit risk perception
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know your exact PGWP expiry date and be prepared to state the remaining duration clearly; 3-year PGWP (granted for programs of 2+ years) is materially different from shorter durations

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Large tech companies and major banks have HR staff familiar with PGWP; small and mid-size companies may not, requiring the candidate to do more education work and accept higher drop-off risk
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Research whether the company has hired international students before; large brand-name employers (Shopify, RBC, TD, major tech) are low-friction; smaller companies require proactive explanation

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Channel choice has a large effect on interview conversion rate; the post documents a clear hierarchy with referrals vastly outperforming mass-apply platforms
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Rank effort allocation as: referrals first, company career pages second, targeted LinkedIn outreach third, Easy Apply / Indeed last; adjust time investment proportionally

decision_factors.why_it_matters: The two major tech markets in Canada have different employer mixes, company sizes, and alumni network density; both were targeted by the OP suggesting dual-city strategy is viable but requires tracking
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess where your alumni network is denser and where your target companies are headquartered; do not default to one city without checking where your referral sources are located

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Choosing Canada over the US for post-graduation employment
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Canadian tech salaries are quoted in CAD; at current exchange rates $112k CAD is approximately $80k USD — a meaningful difference that is frequently overlooked when comparing offers or career trajectories across the border
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students comparing offers from both countries, or those with student debt denominated in USD or another currency

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on LinkedIn Easy Apply and Indeed as primary application channels
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Very low interview conversion rate; high volume of applications produces minimal results relative to the time invested, while higher-signal channels (referrals, direct outreach) are neglected
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Job seekers who default to mass-apply platforms because they feel productive without requiring the social friction of direct outreach

failure_patterns.pattern: Presenting PGWP as a visa requiring employer action, triggering unnecessary HR hesitation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates conflate PGWP with employer-sponsored permits (like LMIA-based work permits) and either phrase their authorization ambiguously or fail to proactively clarify, leaving HR to assume complexity
failure_patterns.consequence: HR screens out the candidate before any substantive evaluation, treating a straightforward hire as a compliance risk
warning_signs: Candidate writes only 'work permit' without specifying open/employer-specific distinction
Candidate waits for HR to ask questions rather than proactively stating 'no employer action required'

failure_patterns.pattern: Wasting time attempting to contest 'citizens/PR only' postings
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates are aware of human rights protections and believe pushing back will yield results; optimism bias about changing a stated policy
failure_patterns.consequence: Time and energy diverted from applications to companies that are genuinely open to PGWP holders; emotional drain without job outcome
warning_signs: Spending more than a few minutes on a posting that explicitly excludes work permit holders
Drafting follow-up messages to explain PGWP to a company that has already stated its preference

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the company a large, brand-name employer or a small/mid-size company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Predicts how much HR education work the candidate will need to do about PGWP, and the likelihood of the application being dropped due to work authorization confusion
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Large employer: proceed normally; HR likely knows PGWP and has processes for it
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Small/mid employer: prepare a one-paragraph plain-language PGWP explanation proactively; anticipate 1-2 rounds of clarification

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you mapped your alumni network before starting job board applications?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is starting from the highest-conversion channel or defaulting to lowest-effort mass-apply
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Good — prioritize activating those connections before any other channel
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Stop applying on job boards temporarily; audit the school alumni directory and LinkedIn alumni filter first

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the remaining duration on your PGWP?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: How much runway you can credibly offer an employer and how urgently you need to also be progressing toward PR status
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: 3 years remaining: relatively low pressure; can be selective
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Under 1 year remaining: employer friction increases significantly; PR pathway urgency is high

industry_realities.common_belief: Hiring international students on a work permit always requires the employer to do something — file paperwork, pay fees, or sponsor the visa
industry_realities.actual_reality: PGWP is an open work permit issued by IRCC directly to the graduate; the employer takes zero administrative action, pays no fees, and files nothing — the candidate can start work immediately on hire
industry_realities.implication: Candidates should lead every work authorization conversation by eliminating this assumption; framing it as 'you don't need to do anything' removes the single biggest source of employer hesitation for smaller companies

industry_realities.common_belief: Canadian tech salaries are comparable to US tech salaries
industry_realities.actual_reality: Canadian salaries are quoted in CAD; the USD/CAD exchange rate creates a meaningful real-terms gap — a $112k CAD offer is approximately $80k USD, a difference of ~30% in purchasing power for internationally benchmarked comparisons
industry_realities.implication: Candidates choosing Canada primarily for immigration certainty should do so with clear eyes about the compensation differential; do not compare raw numbers across currencies

industry_realities.common_belief: Discrimination against work permit holders in hiring is illegal and can be effectively challenged
industry_realities.actual_reality: While the Canadian Human Rights Act has provisions touching on citizenship-based discrimination in employment, enforcement is inconsistent, provincial in scope, and the cost of pursuing a complaint is high; most job seekers who encounter 'citizens/PR only' postings find it more practical to move on
industry_realities.implication: Do not factor in the theoretical legal protection when planning job search strategy; treat 'citizens/PR only' postings as hard stops and reallocate effort

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Writes 'work permit' or 'PGWP' in the authorization field and waits to see if HR asks follow-up questions
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Proactively writes the full explanation including 'open work permit,' 'any employer,' 'no employer action required,' and the exact validity period — eliminates objections before they arise
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: HR at smaller companies will screen out ambiguous work authorization responses; proactive clarity can be the difference between a call and a rejection

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Starts with LinkedIn Easy Apply and Indeed because they are easy to access and create a feeling of productivity through volume
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Starts with alumni network mapping and direct referral activation; treats job boards as supplementary coverage rather than primary strategy
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: The conversion rate difference between referral and mass-apply channels is large enough that misallocating time here is the single biggest efficiency loss in a job search

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Compares Canadian offer numbers directly to US offer numbers without currency conversion
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Converts all offers to the same currency before comparing; understands that Canada's primary value proposition for international students is immigration certainty, not compensation
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Miscalibrated salary expectations lead to poor offer evaluation and poor country-of-work decisions

community_misconceptions.misconception: PGWP requires the employer to do paperwork or pay fees, just like a regular work permit sponsorship
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Most people's mental model of 'work permit' in North America is anchored on employer-sponsored permits (H-1B in the US, LMIA-based permits in Canada); PGWP's open/employer-agnostic nature is a genuine exception that is not intuitively obvious
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: PGWP is an open work permit issued by IRCC to the graduate; the employer has zero administrative role, zero cost, and zero filing requirement — the permit already exists when the candidate applies
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who fail to clarify this lose job opportunities at smaller companies where HR defaults to assuming complexity; companies that might have hired them self-select out based on a false assumption

community_misconceptions.misconception: Canadian tech salary numbers are roughly equivalent to US tech salary numbers
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Job postings in Canada and the US both show numbers in the same range (e.g. $100k–$120k) without the currency prominently flagged; anchoring on the number rather than the currency is cognitively easy
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Canadian salaries are in CAD; at recent exchange rates, $112k CAD ≈ $80k USD — a ~30% real-terms gap for any internationally normalized comparison
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: International students overestimate Canadian compensation relative to US opportunities and make suboptimal job market or country-of-work decisions

real_case_outcomes.situation: CS Master's graduate from Canadian Top-5 university with 3-year PGWP, targeting Toronto and Vancouver tech/finance employers over 3 months
real_case_outcomes.decision: Applied to 90 positions across channels (referrals, company sites, LinkedIn direct outreach, Easy Apply/Indeed); proactively communicated PGWP open work permit status with explicit 'no employer action required' framing
real_case_outcomes.outcome: 12 phone screens, 4 technical interviews, 2 offers; accepted the higher-paying offer at $112k CAD base
real_case_outcomes.lesson: A 90-application, 3-month search with clear work authorization communication and multi-channel strategy yields a ~13% phone screen rate and ~2% offer rate for a strong-profile CS candidate in Canada; referrals and direct outreach materially outperform mass-apply platforms

psychological_barriers.trigger: Encountering a 'citizens/PR only' job posting or HR response
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Injustice sensitivity combined with sunk-cost bias — the candidate has already invested effort in this application and is reluctant to abandon it; awareness of legal protections creates false hope that pushing back will work
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate spends time drafting responses, researching human rights complaints, or attempting to convince HR — all of which yield near-zero job search ROI
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the question from 'can I fight this?' to 'what is the expected return on this hour of effort vs. applying elsewhere?' — makes the opportunity cost concrete and breaks the sunk-cost loop

psychological_barriers.trigger: Comparing a Canadian CAD salary offer to US USD salary numbers
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Anchoring bias on the nominal number; the currency label is less salient than the magnitude, leading to inflated perception of Canadian compensation
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate feels the Canadian offer is competitive without doing the conversion; may fail to accurately weigh the Canada vs. US decision or feel unexpectedly disappointed after starting
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Build the currency conversion step explicitly into any offer evaluation framework; treat CAD and USD numbers as non-comparable until converted

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I deal with employers who are worried about my visa status as a PGWP holder?
reframing_moves.reframe: Your job is to eliminate the employer's assumption of complexity before they form it — not to overcome objections after they arise
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from a reactive posture (defending their status) to a proactive one (preemptively removing friction); changes the mental model from 'visa problem to explain' to 'administrative simplicity to communicate'
reframing_moves.example_language: 「您完全不需要为我申请任何东西，我可以直接入职工作。」(You don't need to do anything for me — I can start work directly.)

reframing_moves.original_framing: I chose Canada for the immigration pathway — how does it compare to the US in terms of career outcome?
reframing_moves.reframe: Canada's value proposition is immigration certainty, not compensation; evaluate the two countries on different dimensions rather than treating them as equivalent alternatives
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Prevents the false equivalence of comparing raw salary numbers across currencies; helps candidates make the decision with accurate expectations rather than discovering the gap post-arrival
reframing_moves.example_language: 「选择加拿大主要是移民路径确定性，不是薪资。」(The reason to choose Canada is immigration pathway certainty, not salary.)
